docs.title: Microsoft Biodiversity: the SPARROW ecosystem for conservation AI
Microsoft Biodiversity
docs.text: Open-source AI for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. Microsoft AI for Good Lab: the SPARROW ecosystem for camera-trap detection, bioacoustic analysis, species classification and field deployment.

docs.title: SPARROW: one ecosystem for AI in biodiversity monitoring
docs.text:
Our work started with MegaDetector, a camera-trap model for finding animals, people and vehicles that is now widely used in conservation. We then built PyTorch-Wildlife to host our detection and classification models in one place. Since then the work has grown to cover bioacoustics, overhead and aerial imagery, field hardware, and the software that moves data from remote sites to the cloud.

We now bring all of it together under one name: SPARROW. Each project has its own repository, so the code is easy to find and each project has a clear owner. This repository is the hub that links them. The table below lists every public project.

docs.title: PyTorch-Wildlife is now SPARROW Playground
docs.text:
We can no longer use the word "PyTorch" in our project names, and our inference now runs on Sparrow Engine, an inference engine written in Rust on ONNX Runtime, with its own Python package (pip install sparrow-engine) and our full model zoo. The PyTorch-Wildlife repository has been renamed and rebuilt as SPARROW Playground: notebooks and small scripts for running the SPARROW tools on your own images, videos and audio, and reusing the code in your own projects. The Playground also has notebooks for live data from SPARROW devices, 4G e-mail cameras and FTPS cameras (through Sparrow Comm), and for serving models over HTTP.

  • Old microsoft/Pytorch-Wildlife links, issues and clones redirect to SPARROW Playground automatically.
  • The old PyTorch-Wildlife code is kept, unmaintained, in the archive/pytorch-wildlife branch and tag v1.3.1.
  • The PytorchWildlife PyPI package ends at 1.3.1 and will get no further updates; we suggest switching to sparrow-engine. To install 1.3.1 in a new environment, add the packages it uses but does not declare: pip install PytorchWildlife==1.3.1 soundfile librosa "setuptools<82".
  • Fine-tuning has moved to dedicated repositories, starting with microsoft/MegaDetector-Classifier.

docs.title: Recent releases
docs.text:
• Sparrow Comm v0.1.0 (November 2026): receivers for SPARROW field data over the device API, Reconyx, e-mail and FTPS. pip install sparrow-comm
  • Sparrow Engine v0.1.32 (November 2026): pip install sparrow-engine, or on macOS brew tap microsoft/sparrow-engine && brew install sparrow-engine
  • SPARROWmini: a small solar-powered field node that runs detection on the device and relays results over a radio mesh to a SPARROW gateway
  • SPARROW Model Zoo Uploader: a toolkit for converting a model, checking that its outputs match the original, and submitting it to the Sparrow Engine model zoo

docs.title: Cite us
docs.text:
When citing work that uses any of the repositories under this umbrella, please cite:

  • Hernandez et al. 2024, Pytorch-Wildlife: A Collaborative Deep Learning Framework for Conservation (arXiv:2405.12930), for the PyTorch-Wildlife framework, Sparrow Engine, SPARROW Playground, or models accessed through them
  • Beery, Morris, Yang 2019, Efficient Pipeline for Camera Trap Image Review (arXiv:1907.06772), for any use of MegaDetector
  • Lavista Ferres et al. 2025, Listening to the Earth in Real Time: SPARROW and the Future of Conservation Technology, for the SPARROW devices (paper in preparation)

See Cite us for BibTeX entries.

docs.title: MegaDetector-Acoustic
docs.text: MegaDetector-Acoustic provides training, inference, and dataset preparation for audio classification in wildlife monitoring. The module is maintained at microsoft/MegaDetector-Acoustic and builds on the bioacoustics APIs of the PytorchWildlife package (PytorchWildlife.data.bioacoustics and PytorchWildlife.models.bioacoustics). That package is no longer updated; its source is archived in the archive/pytorch-wildlife branch of SPARROW Playground.

docs.title: What's included
docs.text:
• CLI scripts for dataset preparation (prepare_dataset.py), training (train.py), and inference (inference.py)
  • ResNetClassifier — PyTorch Lightning module for spectrogram classification (binary and multiclass)
  • Mel-spectrogram preprocessing with optional GPU acceleration
  • Annotation readers (COCO-like JSON), including support for the PteroSet / Raven Pro format
  • MD_AudioBirds_V1 — a pre-trained bird classifier distributed as ONNX for direct inference

See the Sparrow Engine model zoo catalogue for the released acoustic models, including md-audiobirds-v1.

docs.title: Demo
docs.text:
The end-to-end notebook at microsoft/MegaDetector-Acoustic walks through:

  1. Data exploration — annotation counts, species distribution
  2. Inference — run MD_AudioBirds_V1 on real recordings, visualise predictions vs. ground truth
  3. Training — build COCO-style annotations, binary classification (target vs. noise), multiclass classification

It uses recordings from the PteroSet dataset.

docs.title: Projects using this module
docs.text:
• PteroSet — Machine-learning pipeline for detecting and classifying tropical bird vocalisations from passive acoustic monitoring, with leave-one-project-out cross-validation.
  • CookInlet_Belugas — Passive acoustic monitoring for endangered Cook Inlet beluga whales. A two-stage pipeline covering cetacean signal detection and multi-species classification (beluga, humpback, killer whale), plus an active-learning loop for domain adaptation.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/MegaDetector-Acoustic
cd MegaDetector-Acoustic
pip install -r requirements.txt

See the MegaDetector-Acoustic README for requirements, configuration options, training arguments, and output formats.

docs.title: 🤝 Contribution Guidelines
docs.text: Thanks for your interest in contributing! This repository is the hub of the SPARROW ecosystem: it holds the overview, the project list and this documentation site. The code of each project lives in its own repository.

docs.title: How to participate
docs.text:
1. 💡 Find the project you want to work on in the project list.
  2. 📋 Open issues and pull requests in that project's repository. Each repository has its own contribution notes and license.
  3. 📝 For problems with this hub (wrong or broken links, missing projects, outdated descriptions), open an issue or a pull request against main in microsoft/Biodiversity.
  4. 💬 For questions, join us on Discord.

docs.title: Build the docs
docs.text:
This site is built with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs. The pages are in docs/, and the navigation, plugins and redirects for old page URLs are in mkdocs.yml.

  1. Install the dependencies (Python 3.12 is what the deploy workflow uses): 
    pip install -r docs-requirements.txt
  2. Preview the site at http://127.0.0.1:8000/: 
    mkdocs serve
  3. Before opening a pull request, check that the site builds without warnings: 
    mkdocs build --strict

The site/ directory is generated and is not committed. The site is deployed to GitHub Pages by the deploy-docs workflow when changes reach main.

We have adopted the Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct. For more information see the Code of Conduct FAQ or contact us with any additional questions or comments.

docs.title: Project catalogue
docs.text: The Microsoft AI for Good Lab keeps each biodiversity project in its own repository. This page helps you pick a starting point, shows how the projects connect, and links the model zoo. The home page has the short list of repositories.

docs.title: Which project should I use?
docs.text: You want to Start here Also useful Try the tools on your own images, videos or audio SPARROW Playground: notebooks and scripts, no training Quickstart notebook Find animals, people and vehicles in camera-trap images Sparrow Engine with a MegaDetector model from the zoo (pip install sparrow-engine) MegaDetector documentation: model variants, output format and confidence thresholds Name the species in camera-trap detections Sparrow Engine with a camera-trap classifier from the zoo Detection and classification notebook Train or fine-tune a species classifier on your own data MegaDetector-Classifier Detect or identify species in audio recordings Sparrow Engine with an acoustic model from the zoo MegaDetector-Acoustic (the lab's bioacoustic models); bioacoustics notebook Detect wildlife in drone or aerial images MegaDetector-Overhead (OWL models) Overhead models in the zoo Run models from the command line, over HTTP, or from C, C++, Go, Rust or C# Sparrow Engine: spe CLI, Docker HTTP server, C library User manual Receive data from SPARROW devices, 4G e-mail cameras, the Reconyx cloud or FTPS cameras Sparrow Comm (pip install sparrow-comm) Field-data notebooks Deploy a solar-powered AI device at a remote site SPARROW (AI edge device with 4G or satellite uplink) SPARROWmini (small nodes that relay to a SPARROW gateway); SPARROW documentation Add your model to the Sparrow Model Zoo SPARROW Model Zoo Uploader: convert, check outputs against the original, submit Use or read the old PyTorch-Wildlife code The archive/pytorch-wildlife branch of SPARROW Playground (unmaintained) From PyTorch-Wildlife notebook: maps old classes and calls to Sparrow Engine

docs.title: How the projects fit together
docs.text:
1. Capture. A SPARROW device, a SPARROWmini node or a commercial camera trap records images or audio in the field.
  2. Receive. Sparrow Comm collects that data over the device API, e-mail, the Reconyx cloud or FTPS.
  3. Analyse. Sparrow Engine runs models from the Sparrow Model Zoo on it: MegaDetector to find animals, then a classifier for species, or acoustic models for sound.
  4. Explore. SPARROW Playground shows each step in a notebook you can copy into your own code.

Model development happens in the model repositories: MegaDetector, MegaDetector-Classifier, MegaDetector-Acoustic and MegaDetector-Overhead. SPARROW Model Zoo Uploader converts a trained model, checks its outputs against the original, and submits it to the zoo that Sparrow Engine runs.

docs.title: Model zoo
docs.text:
The Sparrow Model Zoo holds the lab's models and third-party models for camera traps, acoustics, overhead and marine imagery, and general use. Each model keeps its own licence, so check it before use, especially for commercial work.

  • Catalogue: the Sparrow Engine model zoo catalogue lists every model with its source, licence and citation. Sections: camera-trap detectors, camera-trap classifiers, acoustic detectors, acoustic classifiers, overhead detectors, marine imagery detectors, licensing at a glance.
  • Model files: the Sparrow Model Zoo on Zenodo. This DOI always opens the latest version.
  • MegaDetector accuracy and model sizes: the MegaDetector model zoo page.
  • Earlier weights: the AI4G-Opossum classifier from PyTorch-Wildlife is not in the Sparrow Model Zoo. Its original weights (OpossumClassification_v0.0.0.ckpt) stay on Zenodo record 10023414.

The model zoo pages that used to live on this site (model_zoo/megadetector/, model_zoo/classifiers/, model_zoo/other_detectors/, model_zoo/bioacoustics/) now redirect to the matching sections of the catalogue.

The Sparrow Engine model zoo catalogue lists the licence, hosting status and commercial-use status of every model. Check it before you use a model.

docs.title: MegaDetector
docs.text:
MegaDetector is Microsoft's open-source AI model for camera-trap conservation — it detects animals, people, and vehicles in camera-trap imagery and filters out blank images, reducing manual review across large datasets. Developed and maintained by the Microsoft AI for Good Lab.

[!IMPORTANT] This page has moved. MegaDetector's canonical home is now microsoft/MegaDetector. Source code, releases, issues, the model zoo, the full version history (V1–V6), benchmarks, and the list of organizations using MegaDetector all live there. This page remains only as a pointer to the canonical repository.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: You want… Go to MegaDetector source, releases, issues, V1–V6 history, benchmarks microsoft/MegaDetector The inference engine that runs MegaDetector and the rest of the model zoo microsoft/SPARROW-Engine Notebooks for running MegaDetector on your own images and videos microsoft/SPARROW-Playground (formerly PyTorch-Wildlife) The biodiversity ecosystem umbrella (all repos, one hub) microsoft/Biodiversity The AI-enabled edge device that runs MegaDetector in the field microsoft/SPARROW

docs.title: Run MegaDetectorV6 quickly
docs.text:
The current generation is MegaDetectorV6 (smaller, faster architectures including YOLOv9, YOLOv10, and RT-DETR; the compact variant is roughly 2% of the V5 parameter count at comparable accuracy). To get started:

  • Follow the Quick Start in the MegaDetector repository.
  • Run the quickstart notebook in SPARROW Playground, which uses Sparrow Engine (pip install sparrow-engine).
  • Try it without writing code in the Hugging Face Space. Full usage, model selection, and the fine-tuning pipeline are documented in microsoft/MegaDetector.

docs.title: MegaDetectorV5 and earlier
docs.text: For MegaDetectorV5 weights and the original repository — primarily developed by Dan Morris during his time at Microsoft — see the archive branch of this repository (formerly microsoft/CameraTraps). Dan continues to actively maintain a community fork at agentmorris/MegaDetector, which remains a valuable resource for the community.

docs.title: Citing MegaDetector
docs.text: A citation.cff is maintained on microsoft/MegaDetector for automated citation tools. Cite Beery, Morris, Yang 2019 — Efficient Pipeline for Camera Trap Image Review for MegaDetector specifically, and Hernandez et al. 2024 — Pytorch-Wildlife for the framework.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: Questions about MegaDetector: open an issue on microsoft/MegaDetector or join the Discord.

docs.title: PyTorch-Wildlife Version 1.2.4
docs.text:
The inference code for the MIT YOLO and Apache RT‑DETR models is now available! To use either one, just load it like any other PyTorch‑Wildlife model:

from pw_detection import MegaDetectorV6MIT, MegaDetectorV6Apache

# MIT YOLO
detector = MegaDetectorV6MIT(
    device=DEVICE,
    pretrained=True,
    version="MDV6-mit-yolov9-e"
)

# Apache RT‑DETR
detector = MegaDetectorV6Apache(
    device=DEVICE,
    pretrained=True,
    version="MDV6-apa-rtdetr-e"
)
Valid versions: - MDV6-mit-yolov9-c - MDV6-mit-yolov9-e - MDV6-apa-rtdetr-c - MDV6-apa-rtdetr-e

You can also try out the full pipeline using the detection_classification_pipeline_demo.py script in the demo folder.

docs.title: SpeciesNet is available in PyTorch-Wildlife for testing!
docs.text: • We have added SpeciesNet into our model zoo, which is compatible with all detection models provided by PyTorch-Wildlife. Please refer to this document for more details!

docs.title: Deepfaune in Our Model Zoo!!
docs.text:
• We are excited to announce the release of the Deepfaune models—both the detector and classifier—in PyTorch-Wildlife, adding to our growing model zoo. A huge thank you to the Deepfaune team for your support! Deepfaune is one of the most comprehensive models focused on the European ecosystem for both detection and classification. It serves as a great complement to MegaDetector, which has primarily been trained on datasets from North America, South America, and Africa. The Deepfaune detector is also our first third-party camera trap detection model integrated into PyTorch-Wildlife!
  • To use the model, you just need to load them as any other PyTorch-Wildlife models: 
    detection_model = pw_detection.DeepfauneDetector(device=DEVICE)
classification_model = pw_classification.DeepfauneClassifier(device=DEVICE)
  • You can also use the detection_classification_pipeline_demo.py script in the demo folder to test the whole detection + classification pipeline.
  • Please also take a look at the original Deepfaune website and give them a star!

docs.title: Deepfaune-New-England in Our Model Zoo Too!!
docs.text:
• Besides the original Deepfaune mode, there is another fine-tuned Deepfaune model developed by USGS for the Northeastern NA area called Deepfaune-New-England (DFNE). It can also be loaded with classification_model = pw_classification.DFNE(device=DEVICE)
  • Please take a look at the orignal DFNE repo and give them a star!

docs.title: PyTorch-Wildlife Version 1.2.0
docs.text:
• In this version of PyTorch-Wildlife, we are happy to release our detection fine-tuning module, with which users can fine-tune their own detection model from any released pre-trained MegaDetectorV6 models. Besides, this module also has functionalities that help users to prepare their datasets for the fine-tuning, just as our classification fine-tuning modules. For more details, please check the readme. Currently the fine-tuning is based on Ultralytics with AGPL. We will release MIT versions in the future. Here is the release page.
  • We have also released additional MegaDetectorV6 models based on Yolo-v10 and RtDetr. We have skipped Yolo-v11 models because of limited performance and architectural gains. Most of the MIT and Apache versions have also finished training but are waiting for internal review before they can be released.
  • We have also updated our AI4G-Amazon model with bigger datasets and it has a better performance compared to previous iterations. Please feel free to test it or fine-tune on it.
  • We will also make a new roadmap for 2025 in the next couple of updates.
  • Special thanks to José Díaz for his great cross-platform app, BoquilaHUB, that is even working on ios and android! Please check his repo out! In the future, we will create a project gallery showcasing projects that use or are build upon PyTorch-Wildlife. If you want your projects to be included, please feel free to reach out to us on

docs.title: Main changes and additions
docs.text:
PyTorch-Wildlife has ended

This page and Past Releases are the release history of PyTorch-Wildlife, which ended with the PytorchWildlife 1.3.1 package and is now SPARROW Playground. Each SPARROW project now publishes its own releases; the home page lists the latest ones.

docs.text: This release has three parts plus a preview of what's next.

docs.title: SPARROW Studio beta
docs.text: SPARROW Studio is our new graphical frontend — data management, inference, analysis, and annotation in one UI. The Windows MSI installer is available from Zenodo: SPARROW Studio Installer (signed). Mac and Linux builds are in progress.

docs.title: MegaDetector-Acoustic
docs.text: MegaDetector-Acoustic is available at microsoft/MegaDetector-Acoustic with CLI scripts for dataset preparation, training, and inference on audio recordings, plus a pre-trained bird classifier (MD_AudioBirds_V1). See the MegaDetector-Acoustic overview, the model zoo catalogue, and the end-to-end demo at microsoft/MegaDetector-Acoustic.

docs.title: MegaDetector-Overhead
docs.text: A new generalized, point-based detection model for overhead imagery. Two variants are released — MegaDetector-Overhead-T and MegaDetector-Overhead-C — listed in the overhead detectors section of the model zoo catalogue. Demo: microsoft/MegaDetector-Overhead.

docs.title: Looking ahead — PW-Engine
docs.text: The future of PyTorchWildlife is PW-Engine, a Rust-based, model-agnostic inference core that powers SPARROW Studio and can also be consumed directly via HTTP, CLI, Python bindings, or a native C library. PW-Engine has since been released as Sparrow Engine (pip install sparrow-engine).
